issues.description: Constructor parameter type mismatch for class 'RollerCoaster': the UML in the problem statement declares the attribute numberOfLoopings as type int (problem expects a constructor parameter of type int for this attribute), but the solution's RollerCoaster constructor signature uses a double parameter (public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, double numberOfLoopings)) and then casts it to int. Meanwhile, the subclass LaunchedRollerCoaster declares its constructor parameter as int and calls super(name, abbreviation, numberOfLoopings). This inconsistency between the UML (int) and the solution implementation (double parameter) is likely to confuse students about the correct constructor signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter type consistent with the UML. Change RollerCoaster's constructor parameter from double to int (e.g. public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings)) and remove the cast. Update any direct references or calls accordingly (e.g. ensure LaunchedRollerCoaster continues to pass an int). Alternatively, if double was intentional, update the UML/problem statement to document numberOfLoopings as double — but prefer changing the constructor to int to match the UML and avoid student confusion.
